entities.summary: Ma Jun, courtesy name Deheng, was a Chinese practical man, inventor, and politician who lived in the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period of China. His most notable invention was the south-pointing chariot, a directional compass vehicle which actually had no magnetic function, but was operated by use of differential gears. It is because of this revolutionary device that Ma Jun is known as one of the most brilliant mechanical engineers and inventors of his day. The device was first demonstrated in 252 CE, during the reign of Cao Pi, the ruler of Cao Wei, and was later adopted by the Eastern Han dynasty as a navigational tool. Ma Jun's invention had a significant impact on the development of navigation and cartography, and his work influenced later inventors and scientists such as Zu Chongzhi and Shen Kuo. Ma Jun's legacy extends beyond his technical achievements, as he also played a key role in the political and social dynamics of the Three Kingdoms period, serving as a high-ranking official in the government of Cao Wei. Ma Jun's life and work serve as a testament to the ingenuity and creativity of Chinese inventors and engineers during the Three Kingdoms period, and his contributions continue to be studied and celebrated by historians and enthusiasts today.
